units.leftText: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, To the twelve tribes of the Dispersion: Greetings. Rejoicing in Trials (Philippians 1:12–20|PHP 1:12-20*)
units.rightText: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are of the Dispersion, greeting.
leftNotes: 1:1 Literally To the twelve tribes in the Diaspora. Originally referring to the Jewish people living outside the land of Israel, the Diaspora is applied here to the Jewish believers scattered abroad.

units.leftText: Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds,
units.rightText: Count it all joy, my brethren, when ye fall into manifold temptations;

units.leftText: because you know that the testing of your faith develops perseverance.
units.rightText: knowing that the proving of your faith worketh patience.

units.leftText: Allow perseverance to finish its work, so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.
units.rightText: And let patience have its perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, lacking in nothing.

units.leftText: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to him.
units.rightText: But if any of you lacketh wisdom, let him ask of God, who giveth to all liberally and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

units.leftText: But he must ask in faith, without doubting, because he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.
units.rightText: But let him ask in faith, nothing doubting: for he that doubteth is like the surge of the sea driven by the wind and tossed.

units.leftText: That man should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.
units.rightText: For let not that man think that he shall receive anything of the Lord;

units.leftText: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
units.rightText: a doubleminded man, unstable in all his ways.

units.leftText: The brother in humble circumstances should exult in his high position.
units.rightText: But let the brother of low degree glory in his high estate:

units.leftText: But the one who is rich should exult in his low position, because he will pass away like a flower of the field.
units.rightText: and the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.

units.leftText: For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant; its flower falls and its beauty is lost. So too, the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.
units.rightText: For the sun ariseth with the scorching wind, and withereth the grass; and the flower thereof falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his goings.

units.leftText: Blessed is the man who perseveres under trial, because when he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love Him. Good and Perfect Gifts
units.rightText: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation; for when he hath been approved, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord promised to them that love him.

units.leftText: When tempted, no one should say, “God is tempting me.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.
units.rightText: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God; for God cannot be tempted with evil, and he himself tempteth no man:

units.leftText: But each one is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed.
units.rightText: but each man is tempted, when he is drawn away by his own lust, and enticed.

units.leftText: Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.
units.rightText: Then the lust, when it hath conceived, beareth sin: and the sin, when it is fullgrown, bringeth forth death.

units.leftText: Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.
units.rightText: Be not deceived, my beloved brethren.

units.leftText: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.
units.rightText: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation, neither shadow that is cast by turning.
leftNotes: 1:17 Or no change or shadow of turning.

units.leftText: He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, that we would be a kind of firstfruits of His creation. Hearing and Doing
units.rightText: Of his own will he brought us forth by the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.

units.leftText: My beloved brothers, understand this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger,
units.rightText: Ye know this, my beloved brethren. But let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:

units.leftText: for man’s anger does not bring about the righteousness that God desires.
units.rightText: for the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.

units.leftText: Therefore, get rid of all moral filth and every expression of evil, and humbly accept the word planted in you, which can save your souls.
units.rightText: Wherefore putting away all filthiness and overflowing of wickedness, receive with meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.

units.leftText: Be doers of the word, and not hearers only. Otherwise, you are deceiving yourselves.
units.rightText: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deluding your own selves.

units.leftText: For anyone who hears the word but does not carry it out is like a man who looks at his face in a mirror,
units.rightText: For if any one is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a mirror:

units.leftText: and after observing himself goes away and immediately forgets what he looks like.
units.rightText: for he beholdeth himself, and goeth away, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.

units.leftText: But the one who looks intently into the perfect law of freedom, and continues to do so — not being a forgetful hearer, but an effective doer — he will be blessed in what he does.
units.rightText: But he that looketh into the perfect law, the law of liberty, and so continueth, being not a hearer that forgetteth but a doer that worketh, this man shall be blessed in his doing.

units.leftText: If anyone considers himself religious and yet does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is worthless.
units.rightText: If any man thinketh himself to be religious, while he bridleth not his tongue but deceiveth his heart, this man’s religion is vain.

units.leftText: Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world.
units.rightText: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this, to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unspotted from the world.

units.leftText: My brothers, as you hold out your faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, do not show favoritism.
units.rightText: My brethren, hold not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.

units.leftText: Suppose a man comes into your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and a poor man in shabby clothes also comes in.
units.rightText: For if there come into your synagogue a man with a gold ring, in fine clothing, and there come in also a poor man in vile clothing;

units.leftText: If you lavish attention on the man in fine clothes and say, “Here is a seat of honor,” but say to the poor man, “You must stand” or “Sit at my feet,”
units.rightText: and ye have regard to him that weareth the fine clothing, and say, Sit thou here in a good place; and ye say to the poor man, Stand thou there, or sit under my footstool;

units.leftText: have you not discriminated among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
units.rightText: do ye not make distinctions among yourselves, and become judges with evil thoughts?

units.leftText: Listen, my beloved brothers: Has not God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom He promised those who love Him?
units.rightText: Hearken, my beloved brethren; did not God choose them that are poor as to the world to be rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he promised to them that love him?

units.leftText: But you have dishonored the poor. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into court?
units.rightText: But ye have dishonored the poor man. Do not the rich oppress you, and themselves drag you before the judgment-seats?

units.leftText: Are they not the ones who blaspheme the noble name by which you have been called?
units.rightText: Do not they blaspheme the honorable name by which ye are called?
leftNotes: 2:7 Or the noble name invoked upon you or the noble name of Him to whom you belong

units.leftText: If you really fulfill the royal law stated in Scripture, “Love your neighbor as yourself,” you are doing well.
units.rightText: Howbeit if ye fulfil the royal law, according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself, ye do well:

units.leftText: But if you show favoritism, you sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.
units.rightText: but if ye have respect of persons, ye commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.

units.leftText: Whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles at just one point is guilty of breaking all of it.
units.rightText: For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet stumble in one point, he is become guilty of all.

units.leftText: For He who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” If you do not commit adultery, but do commit murder, you have become a lawbreaker.
units.rightText: For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou dost not commit adultery, but killest, thou art become a transgressor of the law.

units.leftText: Speak and act as those who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom.
units.rightText: So speak ye, and so do, as men that are to be judged by a law of liberty.

units.leftText: For judgment without mercy will be shown to anyone who has not been merciful. Mercy triumphs over judgment. Faith and Works (Galatians 3:1–9|GAL 3:1-9*)
units.rightText: For judgment is without mercy to him that hath showed no mercy: mercy glorieth against judgment.

units.leftText: What good is it, my brothers, if someone claims to have faith, but has no deeds? Can such faith save him?
units.rightText: What doth it profit, my brethren, if a man say he hath faith, but have not works? can that faith save him?

units.leftText: Suppose a brother or sister is without clothes and daily food.
units.rightText: If a brother or sister be naked and in lack of daily food,

units.leftText: If one of you tells him, “Go in peace; stay warm and well fed,” but does not provide for his physical needs, what good is that?
units.rightText: and one of you say unto them, Go in peace, be ye warmed and filled; and yet ye give them not the things needful to the body; what doth it profit?

units.leftText: So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.
units.rightText: Even so faith, if it have not works, is dead in itself.
leftNotes: 2:17 Literally if it does not have works

units.leftText: But someone will say, “You have faith and I have deeds.” Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds.
units.rightText: Yea, a man will say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: show me thy faith apart from thy works, and I by my works will show thee my faith.

units.leftText: You believe that God is one. Good for you! Even the demons believe that — and shudder.
units.rightText: Thou believest that God is one; thou doest well: the demons also believe, and shudder.
leftNotes: 2:19 Or that there is one God

units.leftText: O foolish man, do you want evidence that faith without deeds is worthless?
units.rightText: But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith apart from works is barren?

units.leftText: Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?
units.rightText: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, in that he offered up Isaac his son upon the altar?

units.leftText: You see that his faith was working with his actions, and his faith was perfected by what he did.
units.rightText: Thou seest that faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect;

units.leftText: And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.
units.rightText: and the scripture was fulfilled which saith, And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned unto him for righteousness; and he was called the friend of God.

units.leftText: As you can see, a man is justified by his deeds and not by faith alone.
units.rightText: Ye see that by works a man is justified, and not only by faith.

units.leftText: In the same way, was not even Rahab the prostitute justified by her actions when she welcomed the spies and sent them off on another route?
units.rightText: And in like manner was not also Rahab the harlot justified by works, in that she received the messengers, and sent them out another way?

units.leftText: As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.
units.rightText: For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, even so faith apart from works is dead.

units.leftText: Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers, because you know that we who teach will be judged more strictly.
units.rightText: Be not many of you teachers, my brethren, knowing that we shall receive heavier judgment.

units.leftText: We all stumble in many ways. If anyone is never at fault in what he says, he is a perfect man, able to control his whole body.
units.rightText: For in many things we all stumble. If any stumbleth not in word, the same is a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body also.

units.leftText: When we put bits into the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we can guide the whole animal.
units.rightText: Now if we put the horses’ bridles into their mouths that they may obey us, we turn about their whole body also.

units.leftText: Consider ships as well. Although they are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the pilot is inclined.
units.rightText: Behold, the ships also, though they are so great and are driven by rough winds, are yet turned about by a very small rudder, whither the impulse of the steersman willeth.

units.leftText: In the same way, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it boasts of great things. Consider how small a spark sets a great forest ablaze.
units.rightText: So the tongue also is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how much wood is kindled by how small a fire!

units.leftText: The tongue also is a fire, a world of wickedness among the parts of the body. It pollutes the whole person, sets the course of his life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.
units.rightText: And the tongue is a fire: the world of iniquity among our members is the tongue, which defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the wheel of nature, and is set on fire by hell.

units.leftText: All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and creatures of the sea are being tamed and have been tamed by man,
units.rightText: For every kind of beasts and birds, of creeping things and things in the sea, is tamed, and hath been tamed by mankind:

units.leftText: but no man can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
units.rightText: but the tongue can no man tame; it is a restless evil, it is full of deadly poison.

units.leftText: With the tongue we bless our Lord and Father, and with it we curse men, who have been made in God’s likeness.
units.rightText: Therewith bless we the Lord and Father; and therewith curse we men, who are made after the likeness of God:

units.leftText: Out of the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, this should not be!
units.rightText: out of the same mouth cometh forth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.

units.leftText: Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring?
units.rightText: Doth the fountain send forth from the same opening sweet water and bitter?
leftNotes: 3:11 Literally Can both fresh and bitter

units.leftText: My brothers, can a fig tree grow olives, or a grapevine bear figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water. The Wisdom from Above
units.rightText: can a fig tree, my brethren, yield olives, or a vine figs? neither can salt water yield sweet.

units.leftText: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show it by his good conduct, by deeds done in the humility that comes from wisdom.
units.rightText: Who is wise and understanding among you? let him show by his good life his works in meekness of wisdom.

units.leftText: But if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast in it or deny the truth.
units.rightText: But if ye have bitter jealousy and faction in your heart, glory not and lie not against the truth.

units.leftText: Such wisdom does not come from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic.
units.rightText: This wisdom is not a wisdom that cometh down from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.

units.leftText: For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every evil practice.
units.rightText: For where jealousy and faction are, there is confusion and every vile deed.

units.leftText: But the wisdom from above is first of all pure, then peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere.
units.rightText: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, easy to be entreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without variance, without hypocrisy.

units.leftText: Peacemakers who sow in peace reap the fruit of righteousness.
units.rightText: And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace for them that make peace.
leftNotes: 3:18 Literally But the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those making peace.

units.leftText: What causes conflicts and quarrels among you? Don’t they come from the passions at war within you?
units.rightText: Whence come wars and whence come fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your pleasures that war in your members?
leftNotes: 4:1 Literally passions warring among your members?

units.leftText: You crave what you do not have; you kill and covet, but are unable to obtain it. You quarrel and fight. You do not have, because you do not ask.
units.rightText: Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and covet, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war; ye have not, because ye ask not.

units.leftText: And when you do ask, you do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, that you may squander it on your pleasures.
units.rightText: Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may spend it in your pleasures.

units.leftText: You adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Therefore, whoever chooses to be a friend of the world renders himself an enemy of God.
units.rightText: Ye adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? Whosoever therefore would be a friend of the world maketh himself an enemy of God.

units.leftText: Or do you think the Scripture says without reason that the Spirit He caused to dwell in us yearns with envy?
units.rightText: Or think ye that the scripture speaketh in vain? Doth the spirit which he made to dwell in us long unto envying?

units.leftText: But He gives us more grace. This is why it says: “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.” Drawing Near to God
units.rightText: But he giveth more grace. Wherefore the scripture saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace to the humble.

units.leftText: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
units.rightText: Be subject therefore unto God; but resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

units.leftText: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
units.rightText: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye doubleminded.

units.leftText: Grieve, mourn, and weep. Turn your laughter to mourning, and your joy to gloom.
units.rightText: Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to heaviness.

units.leftText: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you.
units.rightText: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall exalt you.

units.leftText: Brothers, do not slander one another. Anyone who speaks against his brother or judges him speaks against the law and judges it. And if you judge the law, you are not a practitioner of the law, but a judge of it.
units.rightText: Speak not one against another, brethren. He that speaketh against a brother, or judgeth his brother, speaketh against the law, and judgeth the law: but if thou judgest the law, thou art not a doer of the law, but a judge.

units.leftText: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge, the One who is able to save and destroy. But who are you to judge your neighbor? Do Not Boast about Tomorrow (Proverbs 27:1|PRO 27:1*)
units.rightText: One only is the lawgiver and judge, even he who is able to save and to destroy: but who art thou that judgest thy neighbor?

units.leftText: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, carry on business, and make a profit.”
units.rightText: Come now, ye that say, To-day or to-morrow we will go into this city, and spend a year there, and trade, and get gain:

units.leftText: You do not even know what will happen tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.
units.rightText: whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. What is your life? For ye are a vapor that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.

units.leftText: Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that.”
units.rightText: For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall both live, and do this or that.

units.leftText: As it is, you boast in your proud intentions. All such boasting is evil.
units.rightText: But now ye glory in your vauntings: all such glorying is evil.

units.leftText: Anyone, then, who knows the right thing to do, yet fails to do it, is guilty of sin.
units.rightText: To him therefore that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.

units.leftText: Come now, you who are rich, weep and wail over the misery to come upon you.
units.rightText: Come now, ye rich, weep and howl for your miseries that are coming upon you.

units.leftText: Your riches have rotted and moths have eaten your clothes.
units.rightText: Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are moth-eaten.

units.leftText: Your gold and silver are corroded. Their corrosion will testify against you and consume your flesh like fire.
units.rightText: Your gold and your silver are rusted; and their rust shall be for a testimony against you, and shall eat your flesh as fire. Ye have laid up your treasure in the last days.

units.leftText: Look, the wages you withheld from the workmen who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.
units.rightText: Behold, the hire of the laborers who mowed your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth out: and the cries of them that reaped have entered into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth.

units.leftText: You have lived on earth in luxury and self-indulgence. You have fattened your hearts in the day of slaughter.
units.rightText: Ye have lived delicately on the earth, and taken your pleasure; ye have nourished your hearts in a day of slaughter.

units.leftText: You have condemned and murdered the righteous, who did not resist you. Patience in Suffering (Job 1:1–5|JOB 1:1-5*)
units.rightText: Ye have condemned, ye have killed the righteous one; he doth not resist you.

units.leftText: Be patient, then, brothers, until the Lord’s coming. See how the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the soil — how patient he is for the fall and spring rains.
units.rightText: Be patient therefore, brethren, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it, until it receive the early and latter rain.
leftNotes: 5:7 Literally for it until it receives the early and the late

units.leftText: You, too, be patient and strengthen your hearts, because the Lord’s coming is near.
units.rightText: Be ye also patient; establish your hearts: for the coming of the Lord is at hand.

units.leftText: Do not complain about one another, brothers, so that you will not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door!
units.rightText: Murmur not, brethren, one against another, that ye be not judged: behold, the judge standeth before the doors.

units.leftText: Brothers, as an example of patience in affliction, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
units.rightText: Take, brethren, for an example of suffering and of patience, the prophets who spake in the name of the Lord.

units.leftText: See how blessed we consider those who have persevered. You have heard of Job’s perseverance and have seen the outcome from the Lord. The Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
units.rightText: Behold, we call them blessed that endured: ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord, how that the Lord is full of pity, and merciful.

units.leftText: Above all, my brothers, do not swear, not by heaven or earth or by any other oath. Simply let your “Yes” be yes, and your “No,” no, so that you will not fall under judgment. The Prayer of Faith
units.rightText: But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by the heaven, nor by the earth, nor by any other oath: but let your yea be yea, and your nay, nay; that ye fall not under judgment.

units.leftText: Is any one of you suffering? He should pray. Is anyone cheerful? He should sing praises.
units.rightText: Is any among you suffering? let him pray. Is any cheerful? let him sing praise.

units.leftText: Is any one of you sick? He should call the elders of the church to pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.
units.rightText: Is any among you sick? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord:

units.leftText: And the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick. The Lord will raise him up. If he has sinned, he will be forgiven.
units.rightText: and the prayer of faith shall save him that is sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, it shall be forgiven him.

units.leftText: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail.
units.rightText: Confess therefore your sins one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The supplication of a righteous man availeth much in its working.

units.leftText: Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years.
units.rightText: Elijah was a man of like passions with us, and he prayed fervently that it might not rain; and it rained not on the earth for three years and six months.

units.leftText: Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth yielded its crops. Restoring a Sinner
units.rightText: And he prayed again; and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit.

units.leftText: My brothers, if one of you should wander from the truth and someone should bring him back,
units.rightText: My brethren, if any among you err from the truth, and one convert him;

units.leftText: consider this: Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover over a multitude of sins.
units.rightText: let him know, that he who converteth a sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall cover a multitude of sins.
